messages:
Samir Patel: Quick sync — Oakridge just confirmed they'd like a 3-week POC focused on invoice auto-extract + vendor match. They want measurable KPIs and a security sign-off before pilot.
Priya Desai: Great. Primary success criteria we proposed in call: 1) extraction F1 >= 0.92 on their sample set, 2) vendor-match precision >= 0.90, 3) P95 latency under 350ms for single-doc inference, 4) end-to-end throughput 30 reqs/sec with <5% error rate. Is that still what we want to present?
Jordan Lee: Yep those look right. Can we add an eval for OCR boundary cases? Oakridge has lots of scanned PDFs with rotated pages.
Samir Patel: Good call. Add an OCR robustness bucket (rotated, low-contrast) target: extraction F1 >= 0.85 on that subset.
Elena Morales: Security note from my side: Oakridge requires SSO + SCIM, SOC2 acceptable, optional VPC peering for production. For POC they want encrypted in-transit + at-rest and access logs. Can we include a short tech checklist for the SQA people?
Priya Desai: I'll draft the checklist. For POC infra we can offer Hosted API with IP allowlist + token scoping. If they insist on VPC, that's a Private eval and adds time. We should surface pricing delta.
Samir Patel: Pricing question they asked: rough monthly cost estimate for 50k docs/month during pilot vs projected 1M docs/year if we scale. Anyone have a quick ballpark?
Priya Desai: Ballpark: Hosted inference with our standard mixed-quant model -> ~ $1.2k for 50k docs (mostly small invoices), assuming avg 400 tokens/doc. Annualized at 1M docs -> ~ $20k/mo with reserved capacity discounts and batching. I'll produce a slide with assumptions.
Jordan Lee: Can you also show cost with Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) and with heavier quantization? They care about unit economics.
Priya Desai: Yep — Dedicated typically saves ~30% at that scale. Aggressive int8 quantization might drop quality a bit; we'll show two curves: cost vs F1.
Elena Morales: Security Qs they sent: encryption key management (KMS/HSM), data retention policy, SOC2 report, incident contact, pen-test cadence. I'll attach our standard answers and mark any gaps.
Samir Patel: Ops-bot: kick off POC workspace and upload Oakridge sample set (link shared by Jordan) ->
ops-bot: created workspace oakridge-poc-1854, uploaded 1.2k sample docs, assigned Priya, Samir.
Priya Desai: For the evaluation harness I'll run the following: 1) extraction eval (gold labels) 2) vendor-match precision/recall 3) latency/throughput sweep (with sequence lengths 200/400/800) 4) OCR robustness set. Expected runtime 48 hours once harness starts.
Jordan Lee: Timeline from customer: week 0 sign PO, week 1 ingest + baseline, week 2 tuning and mid-readout, week 3 final readout and SOW for pilot prod. They want final metrics and next-step ask by end of week 3.
Samir Patel: Can we commit to that timeline if security signs off quickly?
Elena Morales: If they accept Hosted with IP allowlist and sign our DPA, security review ~5 business days. VPC would add ~2-3 weeks.
Priya Desai: Deliverables for readout: 1) Final KPI table (F1 / precision / recall / latency p50/p95 / throughput) 2) Failure-mode examples + remediation plan 3) Cost breakdown (hosted vs dedicated) 4) Security checklist + outstanding gaps 5) Proposed SOW & timeline to prod.
Jordan Lee: On metric thresholds, customer said they need F1 >= 0.9 on core fields or they won't proceed. Can we set an internal escalation if we hit 0.88-0.9?
Samir Patel: Yes — if core F1 < 0.9 but >= 0.87, we trigger an engineering escalation and propose label augmentation + small model fine-tune. If <0.87, offer a follow-on eng scope and extended POC.
Priya Desai: Mid-readout plan: quick sync at end of week 2 with sample artifacts and a list of blockers. Final readout doc will include a one-page exec summary for procurement.
Elena Morales: I'll prepare the security one-pager answering their SQ and highlight the SSO/SCIM timeline. Also list any demo data handling restrictions.
Samir Patel: Next immediate actions: 1) Priya to upload evaluation script + cost assumptions (ETA tomorrow EOD) 2) Elena to draft security answers (ETA +2 days) 3) Samir to send SOW draft and commercial comparatives (ETA 48h) 4) Jordan to confirm PO timeline with legal.
Jordan Lee: Confirmed — I'll get PO signed next week if we can meet the security timing.
Samir Patel: Awesome — thanks everyone. I'll book the week-2 mid-readout on Tue 9am PT. :thumbsup:
Priya Desai: booked. :calendar:
Elena Morales: noted. :spiral_calendar:
Jordan Lee: thanks team. Looking forward to the mid-readout.
